newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Repsol Q2 results may signal recovery.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Repsol Q2 results may signal recovery.

text.p: Spain's Repsol posted flat profits for the first half on Wednesday, surprising some who had predicted an up to nine percent fall and setting the stage for something of a comeback by the energy group later in the year, analysts said.

Repsol said net profit after payments to minority shareholders in the six months to June was 61.63 billion pesetas ($388.4 million), compared with 61.45 billion a year earlier. Operating profit rose to 103.85 billion pesetas after 96.05 billion in January to June 1996.

But it was extraordinary profits of 6.01 billion pesetas that boosted the bottom line, with divisional operations mostly as analysts expected. Ailing chemical and gas divisions were still weighing overall income down.
Results at the newly privatised group nevertheless showed a clear improvement in the second quarter versus the first, and this may well be a sign of better things to come, experts said.

"The net income figure is better (than forecast) because of extraordinary results, but the rest of the performance was basically in line (with expectations). Even so there's a clear improvement from the first quarter to the second and we expect that (trend) to continue this year," said Juan Carlos Calvo, analyst at Merrill Lynch in Madrid.
Calvo said Repsol should post an around 12 percent increase in net income by year end, although he may revise his forecast after first half figures.

At the operating level, revenues in both the exploration and refining divisions were boosted by a stronger dollar, and higher crude prices, as well as improved income thanks to new Latin American assets, Repsol said.
The inclusion of Argentine refinery Astra and fatter operating margins helped exploration and production after high value-added fields were incorporated.
Refining and marketing was boosted by bigger international refining margins, the firm said.
But on the negative side was a still-weak chemical division, sapped by maintenance stoppages, with operating results falling to 12.05 bln ptas versus 13.13 bln one year ago.

And a mild winter dented gas division results badly, with consumption underperforming substantially. Unit margins were also lower because of the spread between purchase and sale prices, the firm said. Consequently gas results slumped to 19.60 billion pesetas from 35.98 billion this time last year.
The shares reacted well to the results, and 1415 GMT Repsol was up 170 pesetas, 2.74 percent, to 6,380 pesetas while the Ibex-35 blue chip index was up 1.97 percent to 6,795.63.
Some analysts were predicting that after a period of underperformance in the stock market, Repsol shares will begin to factor in what is expected to be a better second half.
One analyst said his one-year target price was 7,250 pesetas.
